title: Paid KOL Wallet Falsification Report

source.safe_claim: 985monitor published five FOMO-derived CSV snapshots with aggregate leaderboard and common-follow structure as of the May 3, 2026 snapshot.

boundary: Research-only, point-in-time falsification report. Not investment advice. Not a live signal. Not copy-trading guidance. No broker, account, credential, order, fill, execution, position sizing, entry, exit, target, or stop-loss surface is provided.

client_use.intended_buyer: Research desk, fund, founder, market-intelligence team, or crypto operator evaluating source-reported KOL wallet claims.
usable_for: deciding whether a KOL-wallet dataset deserves deeper due diligence
screening claims for provenance, concentration, and baseline gaps
scoping a paid diligence engagement or recurring research report
not_usable_for: redistributing raw wallet-handle mappings without rights review

findings.finding: The page claimed hourly updates, but the inspected page and all five CSV files showed the same May 3, 2026 source timestamp.
findings.business_meaning: This can be sold only as a historical falsification packet until a refresh and archive process exists.
findings.next_safe_action: Set up point-in-time snapshot capture with source timestamp, ingest timestamp, schema hash, and content hash.

findings.finding: No scrape code, source API contract, row-level collection timestamp, wallet-linkage method, or USD valuation source was included.
findings.business_meaning: The report can evaluate source-reported claims but cannot certify wallet ownership, current balances, or future edge.
findings.next_safe_action: Require provenance review before any external paid distribution beyond aggregate research.

findings.finding: The four PnL leaderboards contain 116 unique identities; 72 appear in one window, 31 in two, 11 in three, and only 2 in all four.
findings.business_meaning: Persistence is the first paid-research hook, but the current snapshot cannot prove repeatable skill.
findings.next_safe_action: Test forward-only rank persistence against random active-wallet and volume-weighted baselines.

findings.finding: Top-10 concentration is high: PnL top-10 share ranges from 41.3% to 71.6%, and volume top-10 share ranges from 77.4% to 84.7% across PnL windows.
findings.business_meaning: A small head cohort may dominate apparent results, making the dataset useful for concentration-risk reporting.
findings.next_safe_action: Run leave-top-10-out and identity-cluster stress tests before claiming cohort robustness.

findings.finding: The social/common-follow sheet has 1,065 rows, 44 rows followed by at least 10 top accounts, and 121 rows without a real wallet populated.
findings.business_meaning: The common-follow sheet can support aggregate social-context research, not targeting, contact lists, or coordination claims.
findings.next_safe_action: Keep social fields aggregate or pseudonymous and separate them from any misconduct conclusion.

falsification_verdict.summary: The dataset is commercially useful as a paid falsification and diligence report seed, but it fails promotion gates for live signal, copy-trading, or predictive-performance claims.

proof_gates: Source timestamp and ingest timestamp recorded for every future snapshot.
Every CSV manifest includes filename, row count, schema, byte size, hash, source URL, and provenance status.
Leaderboard fields remain labeled source-reported context, not performance proof.
Common-follow fields remain labeled social context, not identity or coordination proof.
Forward-only outcomes beat random active-wallet and volume-weighted baselines before any edge language is allowed.
Fees, slippage, latency, spread, and capacity stress tests are recorded before monetization claims are increased.
Human and rights review happens before any external sale of derived data.
blocked_outputs: raw wallet resale without rights review
current-balance or ownership claims without source proof
coordination or insider claim without independent evidence
